AI startup ASI valued at $3 billion in latest funding round
Artificial intelligence startup ASI said on Tuesday it had raised $325 million in a funding round valuing the company at $3 billion, amid growing investor appetite for AI software used in real-world applications.

ASI said it would use the proceeds to expand deployments in energy, logistics and military environments and add to its research and engineering teams in Boston Artificial intelligence startup ASI said on Tuesday it had raised $325 million in a funding round valuing the company at $3 billion, amid growing investor appetite for AI software used in real-world applications.
The Series C round was led by Spark Capital, with participation from affiliates of Citadel Securities, Meritech Capital and Craft Ventures, among others
The Boston-based company develops simulation and monitoring software that helps operators forecast disruptions hours, days or weeks in advance across complex systems such as air traffic, power grids and military operations
Advt
"While the broader tech ecosystem spent hundreds of billions teaching AI to manipulate words and generate text, ASI is deeply focused on AI systems that can manage and control physical assets," said Phillip Buckendorf, founder and CEO of ASI
ASI said it would use the proceeds to expand deployments in energy, logistics and military environments and add to its research and engineering teams in Boston
The company secured a five-year, $99 million US Army contract in October and a 12-year, $875 million Federal Aviation Administration contract in June, covering military command systems and air traffic management, respectively

articles.title: SBG Funding Surpasses $3 Billion In Small-Business Financing As 2026 Originations Reach $867 Million
articles.snippet:
SBG Funding has surpassed $3 billion in financing delivered to more than 28,000 U.S. small businesses since its founding in 2017, as the company continues to report rapid growth in annual originations.
The post SBG Funding Surpasses $3 Billion In Small-Business Financing As 2026 Originations Reach $867 Million appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
SBG Funding Surpasses $3 Billion In Small-Business Financing As 2026 Originations Reach $867 Million
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 15, 2026
SBG Funding Surpasses $3 Billion In Small-Business Financing As 2026 Originations Reach $867 Million
SBG Funding has surpassed $3 billion in financing delivered to more than 28,000 U.S. small businesses since its founding in 2017, as the company continues to report rapid growth in annual originations.
The New York City-based financing company originated $867 million during the first nine months of 2026, already exceeding the $794 million originated during all of 2025. SBG Funding said it is on pace to originate approximately $1.15 billion for the full year.
The company’s growth has accelerated significantly in recent years. Annual originations increased from $189 million in 2022 to $422 million in 2024 and $794 million in 2025. SBG Funding originated $7.9 million during its first months of operation in 2017.
Alongside the financing milestone, SBG Funding introduced a new brand identity centered on the tagline “Capital That Keeps Up” and launched a redesigned website. The positioning emphasizes fast, flexible, and responsible financing for established small businesses with steady revenue.
SBG Funding provides capital for purposes including payroll, equipment purchases, working capital, and other operational needs. Through a single application, business owners can be matched with revenue-based financing, term loans, lines of credit, equipment financing, invoice financing, or SBA financing of up to $10 million.
The company said financing decisions typically arrive within 24 hours and applying does not affect an owner’s credit score. Each applicant works with a dedicated adviser who manages the process from application through funding.
SBG Funding operates as both a direct provider of revenue-based financing and a marketplace connecting businesses with financing products through a broader lender network. The company serves businesses across all 50 states, with significant activity in construction, manufacturing, healthcare, retail, food and beverage, and trucking and transportation.
Customers have completed more than 64,000 financing transactions with SBG Funding, including repeat transactions from businesses returning for additional capital. The company said its adviser model allows returning clients to work with people who are already familiar with their businesses and cash flow patterns.
SBG Funding was also named to the Inc. 5000 list of America’s fastest-growing private companies for the fifth consecutive year in 2026, ranking No. 778.
KEY QUOTES:
“Small businesses don’t schedule their opportunities. A contractor wins a bid on Monday and needs equipment by Friday, or a restaurant’s walk-in cooler fails in the middle of July. Capital That Keeps Up is our promise that the money moves as fast as those owners do, and after more than 64,000 transactions, we know what that takes.”
Jeffrey Sachs, Founder And CEO Of SBG Funding
“When a customer comes back for more capital, their adviser already knows the business. That’s a big reason the second decision is often faster than the first.”
Adam Block, Vice President Of Sales And Operations At SBG Funding

articles.title: OrbiMed Raises $3 Billion Across Global And Asia Healthcare Funds
articles.snippet:
OrbiMed has raised $3 billion in commitments across two new private equity funds focused on healthcare and life sciences investments in the U.S., Europe, and Asia.
The post OrbiMed Raises $3 Billion Across Global And Asia Healthcare Funds appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
OrbiMed Raises $3 Billion Across Global And Asia Healthcare Funds
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 15, 2026
OrbiMed Raises $3 Billion Across Global And Asia Healthcare Funds
OrbiMed has raised $3 billion in commitments across two new private equity funds focused on healthcare and life sciences investments in the U.S., Europe, and Asia.
OrbiMed Private Investments X raised more than $1.9 billion to invest in U.S. and European life sciences venture capital opportunities, while OrbiMed Asia Partners VI raised more than $1 billion for healthcare growth equity and venture capital investments across Asia.
Both funds will target companies across biopharmaceuticals, medical devices, diagnostics, and technology-enabled healthcare services. OrbiMed plans to back companies from early development through later growth stages as advances in artificial intelligence, biotechnology, and new therapeutic modalities create additional healthcare opportunities.
The firm highlighted the growing role of AI in drug development and healthcare, the emergence of new therapeutic approaches, and China’s expanding biotechnology industry as major trends shaping its investment strategy.
Investors in the new funds include medical institutions, university endowments, foundations, pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, and family offices. OrbiMed said the capital base includes many long-standing investors that have supported the firm’s previous healthcare strategies.
OrbiMed is led by 20 partners and supported by more than 150 professionals with expertise spanning company incubation, strategy, operations, and finance. The firm operates from 12 locations across major global healthcare markets.
The new funds increase OrbiMed’s investment capacity as the firm manages more than $21 billion in assets. Its broader platform invests across private equity, public equity, and royalty and credit strategies, providing capital to healthcare companies ranging from startups to large multinational corporations.
KEY QUOTES:
“There has never been a more exciting time to invest in life sciences innovation. AI, a proliferation of new therapeutic modalities and China’s emergence as a biotechnology powerhouse are expanding the opportunities to develop transformative treatments. We look forward to helping entrepreneurs turn these advances into leading healthcare companies.”
Carl Gordon, Managing Partner Of OrbiMed
“We are grateful for the continued support of our many long-standing investors. We will work tirelessly over the coming years to meet their high expectations.”
Carter Neild, Managing Partner Of OrbiMed

articles.snippet: Israel Startup Funding Hits $2.77 Billion, Five Firms Raise $1.9 Billion https://ascendants.in/
articles.text:
Israel Startup Funding Hits $2.77 Billion, Five Firms Raise $1.9 Billion
Epil Bodra
| October 1 | Funding Feed , Industry & Events
Share
Israel Startup Funding : Israeli startups closed 28 funding rounds during September 2026, with investors concentrating heavily on cybersecurity, enterprise AI and technologies designed to support autonomous AI agents. Wonderful, Cyera, Island, Upwind and Covenant accounted for nearly 70% of the month’s total investment.
The Israeli tech scene witnessed an inflow of around $2.77 billion into startups in September 2026; however, the breakdown of investments reveals more details about the situation.
Out of 28 rounds of financing, five firms received $1.9 billion together, accounting for almost 69% of the investments made in September. In the rest 23 rounds, an amount of around $870 million was raised by other startups.
Cybersecurity and artificial intelligence featured prominently throughout the month, particularly among businesses developing technologies to help enterprises adopt, operate and secure autonomous AI agents.
Five Mega-Rounds Drive September’s Funding Activity
Enterprise AI startup Wonderful recorded September’s largest transaction, raising $550 million on September 2 at a valuation of $5 billion. The investment came just six months after the company secured $150 million at a $2 billion valuation.
Founded in early 2025, Wonderful has raised more than $800 million to date, expanded into over 35 markets and grown its workforce to approximately 650 employees.
Cybersecurity company Cyera followed with a $400 million investment from Goldman Sachs on September 22. The transaction extended its Series G round, bringing its total funding raised in 2026 to $1.4 billion and pushing its valuation beyond $12 billion.
Island secured another $400 million on September 24, reaching a valuation of $6.4 billion as it expands its enterprise browser technology into a broader control platform for employees and AI agents.
Cloud security company Upwind added $300 million, taking its valuation to $3.8 billion. The figure represents a substantial increase from the $1.5 billion valuation recorded during its $250 million funding round in January.
Completing the five largest transactions was defense technology startup Covenant, which emerged from stealth with $250 million at a valuation exceeding $1 billion.
Together, these investments established the financial weight of September’s largest deals, while funding activity continued across several other technology segments.
Cybersecurity Investors Look Beyond Traditional Protection Tools
One of September’s recurring investment themes was the growing need to secure enterprise environments where AI agents operate alongside human employees.
Several startups attracted funding for technologies addressing this changing security landscape.
Reco raised $55 million with backing from AT&T to expand its security platform as businesses introduce more AI agents into their operations. AIR Security secured $50 million to develop what it describes as a firewall for AI agents.
Cymphony received $25 million in Series A funding for a platform focused on mapping identities, permissions, information and behaviour across people and AI systems.
Meanwhile, Blackstone led a $27 million investment in Huskeys, which is developing an agentic AI layer for web application firewalls.

articles.title: Forbion Raises €2.3 Billion Across Two New Life Sciences Funds
articles.snippet:
Forbion raised €2.3 billion ($2.6 billion) across two new investment funds, marking the largest fundraising in the life sciences venture capital firm's history.
The post Forbion Raises €2.3 Billion Across Two New Life Sciences Funds appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Forbion Raises €2.3 Billion Across Two New Life Sciences Funds
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Forbion Raises €2.3 Billion Across Two New Life Sciences Funds
Forbion raised €2.3 billion ($2.6 billion) across two new investment funds, marking the largest fundraising in the life sciences venture capital firm’s history.
The fundraising exceeded its original target and brings Forbion’s total assets under management to approximately €7.5 billion.
The capital was raised for Forbion Growth Opportunities Fund IV and Forbion Ventures Fund VIII.
Together, the funds are expected to finance approximately 30 biotechnology companies.
Initial investments have already been completed.
Investors include MN, PGGM, KfW Capital, Kauffman Foundation, Eli Lilly and Company, and other existing and new institutional investors.
Growth Opportunities Fund IV will primarily target later-stage biopharmaceutical companies in Europe and North America developing therapies for areas of significant unmet medical need.
Ventures Fund VIII will invest in therapeutics-focused biotechnology companies, including established businesses and newly created ventures built around promising assets and experienced teams.
Over its 20-year history, Forbion has financed 142 companies, including 37 businesses created by the firm.
Portfolio companies have produced 21 approved medical products that have reached more than 1.6 million patients globally.
KEY QUOTES:
“Our successful fundraising gives us significant dry powder in a market characterized by a general shortage of capital. This allows us to select the most exciting biotech companies for investment.”
Sander Slootweg, Managing Partner and Co-Founder of Forbion
“We’ve achieved our largest fundraising to date in a demanding market environment – a powerful endorsement of Forbion’s consistent track record of generating impactful returns.”
Robbert van de Griendt, General Partner, Investor Relations and Impact at Forbion

articles.title: New American Funding Adds Mullinix Mortgage Group With $2 Billion Career Volume
articles.snippet:
New American Funding has added the Mullinix Mortgage Group, expanding the independent mortgage lender’s presence across North Carolina and South Carolina while bringing one of the region’s highest-producing mortgage professionals and his team onto its platform.
The post New American Funding Adds Mullinix Mortgage Group With $2 Billion Career Volume appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
New American Funding Adds Mullinix Mortgage Group With $2 Billion Career Volume
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
New American Funding Adds Mullinix Mortgage Group With $2 Billion Career Volume
New American Funding has added the Mullinix Mortgage Group, expanding the independent mortgage lender’s presence across North Carolina and South Carolina while bringing one of the region’s highest-producing mortgage professionals and his team onto its platform.
The Mullinix Mortgage Group was founded by Will Mullinix, who has more than 20 years of mortgage industry experience and has originated more than $2 billion in mortgages during his career. The group focuses on residential purchase and refinance lending and is licensed across North Carolina, South Carolina, Maryland, Virginia, Tennessee, Georgia, and Florida.
Mullinix was ranked the No. 1 mortgage originator in North Carolina by loan volume by Scotsman Guide in both 2025 and 2026. He was also most recently ranked No. 33 nationwide.
The group serves homebuyers through offices in Charlotte and Wrightsville Beach, North Carolina. Its lending capabilities include conventional, jumbo, physician, first-time homebuyer, bridge loan assistance, FHA, and VA programs. Mullinix Mortgage Group also provides construction and home equity planning for primary residences, second homes, and investment properties.
The full Mullinix Mortgage Group support team and loan officers are joining New American Funding as part of the move. Team members include Taylor Linde, Morgan Wise, Lenzi Moore, Don Walker, and Marty Pizzo.
New American Funding said the addition will provide Mullinix and his team with a broader product platform, technology infrastructure, and operational support as they continue expanding in the Carolinas and other markets. The lender is also preparing to roll out its AI-native Vesta loan origination system in 2027, which it expects will support greater efficiency and scalability for its mortgage professionals.
Mullinix, who was born and raised in Wilmington, North Carolina, later moved to Charlotte and has developed a significant presence across the region. New American Funding sees the team’s local relationships and production record as an opportunity to strengthen its footprint in the Carolinas while supporting the group’s continued growth.
KEY QUOTES:
“New American Funding has a mom-and-pop feel, but with a larger, expansive product platform and national reach. There’s also a strong culture fit and it was just the right move for us and our clients.”
Will Mullinix, Founder Of Mullinix Mortgage Group
“Will Mullinix is the top-producing loan officer in North Carolina, and he got there by putting his clients first every single day. He came to New American Funding to build and scale the Mullinix Mortgage Group, and we have the platform, support, and technology, like our new AI-native LOS Vesta platform rolling out in 2027, to help him do exactly that.”
Pat Bolan, Chief Production Officer At New American Funding
